outcome: Help lenders recover more overdue balances by selecting fair, personalised treatment strategies while identifying customers who need hardship support.
overview: Collections teams often run broad call and message campaigns that are costly, poorly timed and insensitive to customer circumstances. This solution segments overdue accounts using payment, contact, affordability and consent signals; predicts contact and repayment likelihood; recommends the next compliant action with reasons and scripts; and offers approved payment-plan or hardship paths through self-service channels. Vulnerability signals route customers to trained specialists, and high-impact actions stay under policy and human control. A 6–10-week historical proof of value compares strategies against a control group before controlled deployment, targeting higher cure and kept-promise rates, lower cost to collect, and fairer treatment of vulnerable customers.

benefits.text: Increase net cure or recovery by a target 5–15% for the pilot segment
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Lift must be attributed against a randomised or matched control after adjusting for portfolio mix — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce cost per recovered AED by a target 15–30% and avoidable contacts by 20%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on channel-consent quality and completeness of historical contact outcomes

benefits.text: Identify hardship and vulnerability earlier and route those customers to trained specialists under policy
benefits.source: Reference-design control (policy-constrained routing); Redington BFSI catalogue
benefits.limits: Routing is a platform control; detection quality depends on the signals the customer can lawfully use

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); account and contact data stays in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: Contact attempts and outcomes are not recorded, or channel consents are unreliable
notFor.why: Strategy learning and compliant suppression both depend on complete contact and consent history; without them recommendations are guesses

notFor.situation: No hardship policy or trained specialists for vulnerable customers
notFor.why: The design routes vulnerability signals to humans; recommending treatments without that path risks customer harm and conduct breaches

notFor.situation: Controlled testing (champion/challenger or holdout) cannot be approved
notFor.why: Recovery lift cannot be honestly attributed without a control design; an unattributable pilot proves nothing

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns treatment policy, customer conduct and hardship approval · Duration: 6–10 weeks PoV; 14–24 weeks to production
Delivery pod: Partner technical lead + project manager, vendor platform specialist, data scientist; customer collections sponsor, conduct/compliance owner, data owner, finance, contact-centre lead, security and privacy approvers, hardship lead · Support model: Business-hours or extended support with severity-based targets; partner first line with vendor escalation; optional managed strategy service
1) Discovery, baseline and control design
2) Data preparation and strategy build
3) Historical simulation
4) Channel integration and conduct/security review
5) UAT and agent training
6) Controlled launch, stabilisation and handover
deliverables: Statistically credible net-recovery lift or agreed leading indicator achieved
Consent suppression proven in every integrated channel
Hardship routing tested end to end
Audit and monitoring active; agents trained and signed off
languages: English delivery; Arabic customer communications and self-service journeys supported
